description:
src/lib.rs lines 360-378: Display is implemented on IdentityError with hard-coded user-facing strings:

  'pkix-identity functionality not yet implemented'
  'malformed identity input'
  'no Subject Alternative Name entry matched the identity'
  'certificate has no Subject Alternative Name extension'
  'certificate Subject Alternative Name extension is malformed'

Once shipped, callers will grep these strings in logs, regex them in test assertions, and write user-facing copy that mirrors them. This makes the strings part of the de-facto API surface even though no docstring promises stability.

Two ways forward:

1. Document that Display output is not version-stable, and rely on the variant name (Debug) for programmatic dispatch. This is the most-common Rust convention; rustdoc on Display should state 'Format strings are not part of the API contract.'

2. Promise version stability and treat string changes as breaking. This is the harder commitment but matches what serde-deserialization-from-localized-strings callers might expect.

Today's docstring on IdentityError says nothing about Display stability. Recommend (1) with an explicit docstring.

Lower priority because either decision is OK as long as it's made and documented; doing nothing is the bad outcome.

Severity P3: doc bug, easy fix, no engineering blocker.
title: Display impl on IdentityError commits to message strings as part of public surface
